editorial:
If you love a good mystery with a dash of action, this Detective Conan adventure drops you into a thrilling chase. The story kicks off when Phantom Thief Kid sends a message that he plans to steal a valuable Japanese sword from the wealthy Onoe family in Hakodate, Hokkaido. Conan and Heiji Hattori are in town, so they jump on the case to catch Kid. Things get complicated when the family lawyer turns up murdered in the warehouse district, killed by a sword. Suddenly the treasure hunt becomes a murder investigation, and you are pulled along through cherry blossoms and northern streets.

What really stands out is how the movie balances humor, suspense, and fast action without feeling too heavy. The animation looks sharp, the pacing keeps you on your toes, and the chemistry between Conan and Heiji adds fun buddy-cop energy. On the downside, the plot can feel crowded with so many characters and clues. If you enjoy anime mysteries or crime thrillers, this one is a blast.
endingExplained: In the final act, Conan and Heiji uncover that the murdered lawyer knew the location of the Onoe family's hidden treasure. The real killer is not the suspected arms dealer but someone closer to the family who wanted the treasure for themselves. Kid the Phantom Thief appears, steals the sword, but leaves a clue that helps Conan solve the case. The treasure is revealed to be a historical artifact, and the culprit is arrested as cherry blossoms fall over Hakodate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves anime mysteries and crime thrillers
